newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turk-Iran gas line construction to start in March.
newsitem.headline: Turk-Iran gas line construction to start in March.

text.p: Brushing aside criticism from the United States, Turkey's energy minister said on Tuesday Tehran and Ankara in March will start building a pipeline to carry Iranian gas to Turkey.

"Iran and Turkey will lay the ground at the same time for the construction of the gas pipeline in March at the joint border," Turkish Energy Minister Recai Kutan told reporters during a joint news conference with visiting Iranian Oil Minister Gholamreza Aghazadeh in Ankara.

"The pipeline will carry three billion cubic metres of Iranian gas from the beginning of 1998, one year earlier than the original project," he said. "Later, from 2005, the purchases will be 10 billion cubic metres."
U.S. State Department Spokesman Nicholas Burns on Monday said Washington did "not believe it is a good idea for any country to have normal relations with Iran".

Kutan slammed Washington's position on the deal, saying he did not believe the project would breach a U.S. law setting penalties firms investing $40 million or more in a year in energy projects in Iran and Libya.

"America made its suggestion. That's fine. But we need energy and go ahead according to our national interests. I myself don't believe Iran is a terrorist country." said Kutan, a member of the Islamist wing of the coalition government.
He said Iran and Turkey would invite tenders separately later this month to build segments of the pipeline in their territories.
"We will give the contractor consortia two months to submit their bids and later assess the bids for one month. We will choose the contractor in March, when the construction will begin," he said.

He said Turkey would initially tender for the 250-km (155-mile) extending from the border to its eastern province of Erzurum and Iran for the 270-km (168-mile) segment from Tabriz to the Turkish border. Both lines will be 40 inches in diameter.
"The initial part in Turkey will cost about $200 million and so will the part in Iran. Both countries will finance the pipeline projects themselves," he said.

Turkey will later hold another tender after the Iranian gas reaches Erzurum to carry it to Ankara through a 800-km (500-mile) pipeline whose capacity will be determined after talks for additional 16 billion cubic metres a year from Russia through its eastern border are concluded.
"The Russian gas, if agreed, will also reach Erzurum through a pipeline from Georgia to Erzurum. Therefore a larger line may be needed for Erzurum-Ankara segment," Kutan said.
Aghazadeh said Turkey's payments for gas would be in cash but both ministers refused to disclose the exact price.
"The (two-way) trade volume between Turkey and Iran is planned to rise to $2 billion a year and Turkey's payments will be included in this amount," Aghazadeh said.

Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan's Islamist coalition government, which signed the $23-billion, 23-year gas agreement in Tehran in August, has vowed to improve Turkey's relations with Islamic countries, especially with Iran.
